subject: Re: Follow-up on 2/17 incident — request: automatic rollback on SLO breach
body:
From: Alicia Tran <alicia.tran@blueskyhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@blueskyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Follow-up on 2/17 incident — request: automatic rollback on SLO breach

Rafael,

Thanks again for jumping on the bridge yesterday.

As discussed, we need Redwood to automatically roll back a model version when latency and/or error rates exceed our SLOs during a rollout. The manual rollback process took too long for us and we had measurable customer impact.

Requirements (high level):
- Trigger: p95 latency + 5xx error rate (we can provide exact definitions if needed)
- Scope: per route + region (we’ve seen one region degrade while others look fine)
- Action: revert traffic split back to prior stable version
- Safety: avoid flapping / repeated rollbacks; include cool-down
- Visibility: audit trail + who/what triggered rollback (we need this for internal change management)

Timeline ask: we’d like a committed plan for availability and a rough ETA. Ideally this is in place before our next set of model upgrades in March.

Attaching our incident summary and our current SLO targets/routes.

Attachment: BlueSkyHealth_Incident_2025-02-17_Summary.pdf
Attachment: bluesky_slo_targets_and_routes.xlsx

Best,
Alicia Tran
Director, Platform Reliability
BlueSky Health


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Tran <alicia.tran@blueskyhealth.com>
Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@blueskyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 10:01 AM
Subject: Re: Follow-up on 2/17 incident — request: automatic rollback on SLO breach

Alicia — understood, and thank you for sending the summary + SLO workbook.

We have an in-flight initiative to integrate rollback automation with our latency/error SLO monitors (auto-rollback on SLO breach), including guardrails to prevent flapping.

A few quick clarifications so we can make sure we match your change-management needs:
1) Rollback trigger logic: do you want fixed thresholds (e.g., p95 > X ms for Y minutes) or “worse than baseline” during rollout (candidate vs current stable)?
2) Minimum traffic: are there low-volume routes where the signals are noisy? (we usually add minimum request rate / sample count)
3) Failure mode: if monitoring is delayed/unavailable, do you prefer fail-open (don’t roll back automatically) or fail-closed (treat unknown as breach)?

I’m looping in our SRE and PM owners internally to confirm a timeline and what we can commit for March.

Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference


From: Alicia Tran <alicia.tran@blueskyhealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@blueskyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 11:08 AM
Subject: Re: Follow-up on 2/17 incident — request: automatic rollback on SLO breach

Rafael,

Answers inline:

1) Prefer “worse than baseline” where possible. We’ve had planned capacity shifts where absolute latency can move slightly, but the candidate clearly regressed vs the stable.
   - That said, we’d like to keep an absolute ceiling as a backstop.

2) Yes on minimum traffic. A couple routes have bursty traffic. We can accept a warm-up period during a rollout (e.g., first 10–15 minutes) before automation can trigger.

3) Strong preference for fail-open on monitoring outages. We’d rather page a human than have automation do something surprising when the signal is unknown.

Also: region-specific thresholds matter to us. us-east is more sensitive because it serves the majority of end users.

Thanks,
Alicia


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 11:32 AM
Subject: Fwd: BlueSky Health follow-up — auto rollback on SLO breach requirements + March timeline ask

Forwarding BlueSky’s ask post-incident (2/17). They’re requesting auto-rollback tied to latency + 5xx SLOs during model rollouts.

Key requirements from customer:
- Trigger on p95 latency + 5xx error rate
- Per route + per region (explicitly called out)
- Prefer “worse than baseline” vs fixed thresholds, with an absolute ceiling as backstop
- Minimum traffic + warm-up window (10–15 min ok)
- Avoid flapping (cooldown)
- Fail-open if monitors are stale/unavailable
- Must have audit trail + “who/what triggered rollback” (change management)
- Timeline: wants this before March upgrade wave; asked for committed plan + rough ETA

Attaching what they sent (incident summary + SLO workbook). Also linking their open escalation.
- SUP-18421
- HubSpot company-49201

Can you both sanity-check what we can commit (internal GA vs allowlist) and a realistic timeline to communicate back?

— Rafael

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 12:06 PM
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueSky Health follow-up — auto rollback on SLO breach requirements + March timeline ask

Thanks. This matches what we’ve been pushing for since the Feb regression postmortem.

From SRE perspective, their preferences are aligned with what we consider “safe defaults”:
- fail-open on monitor outage (unknown verdict)
- warm-up + minimum traffic guards
- cooldown to prevent flapping
- baseline comparison (candidate vs stable) + absolute ceiling

Timeline: I don’t want to overcommit for March GA. But we could likely support an allowlisted early access in March for a limited set of routes/regions if the control plane team is on track.

Paula — can you confirm whether product is okay with early access + explicit disclaimers?

Sean


From: Paula Mendes <paula.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 1:24 PM
Subject: Re: Fwd: BlueSky Health follow-up — auto rollback on SLO breach requirements + March timeline ask

Agree with Sean.

Product stance:
- We can commit to: (1) design complete + (2) early access allowlist in March, assuming telemetry labels/monitor IDs for their routes are already in good shape.
- GA is more likely early/mid April given UI + audit logging + hardening.

For customer-facing framing:
- Make clear that early access requires: monitor correctness validation + limited scope + oncall oversight.
- We should explicitly set expectations on “per-region thresholds” (supported in policy config) and baseline comparison semantics.

Rafael — if you want, I can share a short paragraph you can paste to the customer with the above.

Paula
Sr PM, Rollouts & Reliability


From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Tran <alicia.tran@blueskyhealth.com>
Cc: Devon Price <devon.price@blueskyhealth.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 4:41 PM
Subject: Re: Follow-up on 2/17 incident — request: automatic rollback on SLO breach

Alicia,

Following up with an actionable plan and timeline.

We’re actively building “auto-rollback on SLO breach” for rollouts, integrating rollback automation with our latency + error SLO monitors. The behavior you outlined (baseline comparison + absolute ceiling, warm-up/min traffic, cooldown, per-region scope, fail-open on monitor outage, and audit trail) is in-scope for the design.

Proposed timeline:
- March: early access (allowlisted) for a limited set of routes/regions for BlueSky, with SRE oversight and explicit guardrails enabled (warm-up/min traffic/cooldown + fail-open on unknown).
- Early/Mid April: broader availability after we complete the remaining hardening + Console UI + audit logging.

Next steps (if you’re aligned):
1) You send us the final SLO thresholds you want for p95 latency + 5xx by route/region (we can start from the sheet you attached).
2) We schedule a 30-minute working session next week to confirm monitor definitions/labels and agree on rollout policy defaults for BlueSky.

If you can share a few “must cover” routes for March early access, we’ll prioritize those first.

Rafael Mendes
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
